neighbours.label: continuation pieces of a few fixed religious or scientific names (the second digit of a Luke chapter, 'an' in Rosh Hash|an|ah, 'opus' in Rhiz|opus), as against other chapter numbers, holidays and moulds
fire: The story of the rich man and Lazarus comes from Luke 16 in most Bibles.
Our synagogue holds a family service on Rosh Hashanah every autumn.
Fruit left out too long can grow Rhizopus, a fast black mould.
The sermon on Sunday was based on Luke 18 and the persistent widow.
Many families blow the shofar at Rosh Hashanah to mark the new year.
The lab grew Rhizopus on bread to study how spores spread.
In the reading plan, week three covers Luke 12 and Luke 13.
Shops close early before Rosh Hashanah in parts of the city.
quiet: The story of the rich man and Lazarus is often told at funerals.
Our synagogue holds a family service on Hanukkah every winter.
Fruit left out too long can grow Penicillium, a green mould.
The sermon on Sunday was based on chapter 18 of the novel.
Many families light candles at Christmas to mark the season.
The lab grew yeast on bread to study how cells divide.
In the reading plan, week three covers pages 12 and 13.
Shops close early before New Year in parts of the city.
